earn.title: Earn Merits
earn.subtitle: You earn Merits whenever you give economic value to society. Here are the three main ways:
earn.taxes_desc: Register purchase receipts **from stores in Slovakia** and earn Merits for the VAT charged.
earn.charity_desc: Earn Merits for a gift to a verified nonprofit or public-benefit organisation of your choice
earn.how_intro: Civic records Merits as **labor-hour equivalents** — a non-transferable measure of value you already gave to society (euros paid as tax or gift, or volunteer work). **10 ME = 1 hour** of work. Merits are recognition, not money you can reclaim.
earn.how_taxes: For taxes, the **VAT** (taxed euros) on your receipt is divided by the national average hourly wage. The resulting number of equivalent hours is multiplied by **10** to get Merits (ME).
earn.how_charity: For gifts, after the gift is **verified**, the **euro amount** is divided by the national average hourly wage. The resulting number of equivalent hours is multiplied by **10** to get Merits (ME). Merits are credited after verification — not at the moment of payment.
earn.how_volunteer: For volunteering, the **hours you report** are already labor-hours. They are multiplied by **10** to get Merits (ME).

volunteer.nace_ai_tips_title: Tips for better NACE code matching
volunteer.nace_ai_tip_1: Lead with the verb — what you did (contacted, cleared, taught, edited…), not just a noun or tool.
volunteer.nace_ai_tip_2: Describe your role, not the other party’s industry. Contacting a newspaper is outreach, not newspaper publishing.
volunteer.nace_ai_tip_3: Name the kind of work in plain language (media outreach, trail maintenance, map data editing…).
volunteer.nace_ai_tip_4: One concrete action in 1–2 sentences beats a vague short line like “I wrote an email”.
volunteer.nace_ai_tip_5: Don’t rely on the project alone — say the action again in this description.
